title: Recover from a frozen bank account or bank failure
summary: Confirm whether the account is frozen or the bank has failed, assess exposure under the applicable deposit-protection scheme, and arrange continuity for essential payments. Work through the bank’s compliance process or the relevant resolution authority and retain evidence of any claims.

countryViews.title: Recover from a frozen bank account or bank failure in United States
countryViews.summary: Frozen account or failed bank, the problem is the same: payroll has to go out, in every country. Confirm what happened. Work out how much is covered by deposit insurance (US: FDIC covers $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category; the UK, German, French, and Indian caps are in the geo notes). Open a second operating account so the payments that cannot bounce don't. Then the paths split. A compliance freeze is a documents conversation with the bank: KYC and beneficial ownership. A bank failure is a receivership you track and file claims against for the uninsured balance (in the US, with the FDIC). Moving banking rails mid-crisis can be undone, but at real cost.

parts.title: Confirm whether the account is frozen or the bank has failed

execution.rationale: Compare the supplied bank notice with the official failed-bank information to identify the event actually reported.

geoResolutions.label: Confirm what happened: a compliance freeze notice from the bank, or the bank itself failing (US: the FDIC failed-bank list; your country's resolution authority otherwise)

parts.title: Assess balances against the applicable deposit-protection limit

execution.rationale: Calculate the exposure from supplied balances and the verified applicable protection rules for adviser review.

geoResolutions.label: Size the exposure: balances against your deposit-protection limit (US: FDIC's $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category — other schemes in the geo notes)

parts.title: Triage the next payroll run and the payments that cannot bounce

execution.rationale: Prioritize the supplied payroll and payable schedule against available liquidity for finance's release decisions.

parts.title: Open a backup operating account at a second bank

execution.rationale: The owner completes the backup bank's online onboarding and personal verification, checking funding and access before relying on the account.

parts.title: Re-point the rails: processor payouts in, payroll and vendor payments out

execution.rationale: The finance and payroll administrators change the approved bank destinations in each actual provider and verify payouts and outgoing payments through the account records.

parts.title: If it's a compliance freeze: ask what triggered the review and supply the KYC/UBO documents the bank asks for

execution.rationale: The account owner exchanges the requested KYC and ownership records with the frozen bank through its secure case channel.

parts.title: If the bank failed: track the bank resolution and file claims for uninsured balances

execution.rationale: The finance owner tracks receivership notices and submits the uninsured-balance claim through the receiver's applicable case channel with reviewed balance evidence.

geoResolutions.label: If the bank failed: track the receivership (US: the FDIC's) and file the claim for uninsured balances

parts.title: Wait for the freeze review or the receivership distributions

execution.rationale: The finance owner follows the bank or receivership's case communications remotely and records available funds, requests and decisions as they arrive.

metadata.trigger: Your operating account is frozen by the bank's compliance review, or the bank itself fails.
metadata.supportReason: Opening the backup account is KYC-gated, the freeze conversation is with the bank's compliance team, and the FDIC claim is theirs to process. An agent can size the insurance exposure from your balances; it cannot unfreeze an account.

geoNotes.summary: If a UK-authorised bank fails, the FSCS protects £85,000 per depositor per bank and aims to pay most depositors within days; a compliance freeze is the same KYC/UBO documents conversation with the bank — and standing up a second operating account for payroll is the same first move.

The statutory Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken (EdB) compensates €100,000 per depositor per bank (the EU deposit-guarantee floor) and contacts depositors after a failure; compliance freezes are worked out with the bank's own team under BaFin supervision.

The FGDR guarantees €100,000 per depositor per bank and targets compensation within seven working days of a failure; a gel du compte lifts on the bank's KYC questions being answered, not on a form — the backup-account move is identical.

DICGC insurance covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal plus interest), and RBI moratoria on stressed banks have historically capped withdrawals for months — which makes the second-account triage even more important than in the US.

If an SDIC scheme member bank fails, insured deposits are covered up to S$100,000 per depositor per member by the Singapore Deposit Insurance Corporation; a compliance freeze is the same KYC/UBO documents conversation with the bank.
